name: Saanich

seo.title: Landscaping in Saanich, BC: Lawns, Gardens & Trees | RNC
seo.description: Lawn and garden care, irrigation and tree work across Saanich, from Gordon Head to Prospect Lake, planned around protected and nesting trees. Get a free quote.

cardSummary: Suburban lots under big firs, farmland and lakeside acreage, with some of the region’s lowest tree-protection thresholds.
intro: Saanich is big and varied: suburban streets in Gordon Head and Cordova Bay, farmland around Blenkinsop, lakeside rural lots near Prospect Lake, and stratas and plazas along the Royal Oak and Shelbourne corridors. Each needs a different plan.

Saanich protects Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew from just 2 m tall or 4 cm across, plus trees with raptor, osprey or heron nests, and a permit is needed before cutting a protected tree even if it is dead. See [grounds maintenance](/services/grounds-maintenance/) or [request a free quote](/free-quote/?area=saanich).
localRulesIntro: Saanich sets size thresholds by species: native trees are protected almost from the sapling stage, large conifers from 30 cm, and nest trees regardless of size. Dead or dying trees are not exempt.

localNotes.title: Saanich Tree Protection Bylaw
localNotes.text: Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw protects Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew at 2 m tall or 4 cm diameter; Douglas-fir, grand fir, bigleaf maple and western redcedar at 30 cm diameter; any other tree at 60 cm; plus replacement, significant and nesting trees. A tree cutting permit is required before cutting a protected tree, even if dead or dying, and the bylaw also covers pruning or damaging protected trees.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Fir shade and moss
conditions.body: Gordon Head, Cordova Bay and Broadmead have many large Douglas-firs. Their shade and needle litter favour moss over grass, so lawn plans here usually include moss control, aeration or giving some lawn back to shade beds.

conditions.title: Deer in suburban gardens
conditions.body: Deer browse gardens in many Saanich neighbourhoods, so new planting is chosen for deer resistance or protected while it establishes.

conditions.title: Rural edges, lakes and farmland
conditions.body: Around Prospect Lake and Blenkinsop, lots are larger, some sit near lakes, streams or farm fields, and not every rural property may draw on the regional supply. Confirm yours before relying on the CRD lawn days.

conditions.title: Nesting season matters
conditions.body: Because nest trees are protected, spring and early-summer tree work in wooded Saanich lots should start with a look for active nests.

topServices.why: Suburban lawns under big firs need a steady routine of mowing, moss control and bed care to stay usable.
Low protection thresholds and nest-tree rules mean even modest pruning or removals benefit from a permit check first.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Lawn, bed and hedge care for suburban lots, with moss plans for shady yards under big firs.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Front and back garden builds on suburban lots, and planting on rural properties.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Start-up, repair and winterization for home and strata systems across Saanich.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Pruning and removals planned around Saanich's protected species and nesting trees.

jobNotes.title: Laurel hedge reduced after a nest check
jobNotes.body: An overgrown laurel hedge was reduced in two passes, the first left until a spring check confirmed there were no active nests in the adjoining firs.

jobNotes.title: Townhouse start-up with a zone map
jobNotes.body: A townhouse strata’s system was started up in spring, broken heads were replaced, and council was given a simple map of which zone waters which bed.

cta.heading: Get a free quote in Saanich
cta.body: Tell us your neighbourhood and whether the lot is suburban or rural. If native trees or big firs are near the work, say so and we will plan the permit question in from the start.
